result:
`pricebook.py` has 150 rules, and 10 of them didn't match their docstrings. I fixed all 10.

After the fixes, all 150 rules give the result their docstring describes. I checked each one with a script against a grid of quantities from 0 up past its threshold, plus large orders, and a range of unit prices. Every rule also checks for negative inputs.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 117 (whole) | Applied the cap to the price before taking 8% | Take 8% first, then cap the discount at 30,000 won |
| 25, 77 (marginal) | Same: applied the cap to the price before taking the percentage | Take the percentage first, then cap the discount |
| 45 (marginal) | The cap only kicked in when the discount was over 200,000 won, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always cap at 100,000 won |
| 147, 49 (marginal), 89 (whole) | Used `round()`, which rounds to the nearest won | Changed to `//` so the discount is rounded down to the won |
| 134 (`> 30`), 92 (`> 20`), 76 (`>= 51`) | The discount started one unit above the threshold, so an order of exactly the threshold quantity got no discount | Changed to `>= threshold` |

There's a backup of the original file at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.bak`.

STATUS: DONE
